d.request: Include executions whose `expirespot`, compared as text, is strictly greater than '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and strictly less than '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'; group by `ordersmark` to calculate each order’s average non-null `remaincount` and execution count, then return one row containing the average of the non-null per-order averages and the sum of the per-order execution counts, without rounding.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_remaincount) AS avg_per_order_remaincount, SUM(execution_count) AS total_execution_count FROM (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remaincount, COUNT(*) AS execution_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) AS per_order

c.request: For order executions with an expiry time (`expirespot`) between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and work out each order's average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and its number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding. Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are excluded, so only expiry times strictly between the two bounds count.
c.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_unfilled_quantity, COUNT(*) AS execution_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) SELECT AVG(avg_unfilled_quantity) AS average_unfilled_quantity, SUM(execution_count) AS total_execution_count FROM per_order;

b.request: Select executions whose `expirespot`, compared as text, is strictly greater than '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and strictly less than '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'; group by `ordersmark`, calculate each group’s average non-null `remaincount` and execution count, then return one unrounded row containing the average of the non-null group averages and the sum of the group counts.
b.sql: WITH execution_groups AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remaincount, COUNT(*) AS execution_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) SELECT AVG(avg_remaincount) AS average_group_remaincount, SUM(execution_count) AS total_execution_count FROM execution_groups

a.request: Looking only at order executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) falls between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', with both endpoints excluded (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and, for each order, compute the average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and the number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding.
a.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remaincount, COUNT(*) AS execution_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) SELECT AVG(avg_remaincount) AS avg_of_order_averages, COALESCE(SUM(execution_count), 0) AS total_execution_count FROM per_order
